scenes.headline: Traditional foods deserve [a modern store.]
strike: Banners only a developer could change

vo.text: Mithra Whole Foods sells millets, cold-pressed oils, ghee and traditional foods, and it was running on an ageing template store.
So I rebuilt it as a headless store.

scenes.title: Mithra Whole Foods
scenes.tagline: A Next.js storefront on a Medusa v2 commerce backend.

vo.text: The full path, from catalogue to payment, works end to end.

scenes.headline: Find it in [one search.]
bullets: Categories for millets, oils, ghee and more
Search runs inside the Medusa backend
No third-party index to pay for or sync

vo.text: Shoppers browse by category, or search.
And search runs inside the Medusa backend itself, so there's no external search service to pay for or keep in sync.

scenes.headline: An optimistic cart and a [four-step checkout.]
bullets: Rolls back with a message if the backend says no
Address, shipping, payment, review — paid with Stripe

vo.text: Add to cart updates instantly, then reconciles with the backend, and rolls back with a clear message if something can't be added.
Checkout runs in four steps, address, shipping, payment and review, with Stripe taking the payment.

scenes.headline: The same store, [in your pocket.]
bullets: A homepage CMS the client edits
Live preview in the admin before publishing

vo.text: It's built for phones first, and a custom homepage module, with a live preview in the admin, lets the client change banners and featured collections without a developer.

scenes.headline: Measure first. [Then fix the right thing.]

nodes.title: Medusa v2 backend
nodes.sub: On Railway; search, CMS, reviews, Easyship

vo.text: Under the hood: a Next.js storefront on Vercel, the Medusa backend on Railway, Neon Postgres, and Stripe.
When pages felt slow, I measured instead of guessing. Every database query was costing two hundred and ninety milliseconds, because the backend and the database sat on different continents.
So the fix is the region, not a new database vendor.
Traditional foods, in a modern store.
Read the full case study, and see how it was built.
